_notes.scope: Deterministic stage only (applyQueryUnderstanding without a place vocabulary): residualQ is what reaches Meili BEFORE place resolution, so place words (Toronto, Canada, in London) are still in it; place parsing has its own tests.
_notes.titles: Title normalisation is out of scope: residualQ keeps typed words. JOBS_SYNONYMS (meilisearch.ts) already contains pm -> product manager, project manager (one-way) and sre -> site reliability engineer, so cases 3, 15, 18, 22, 30 are expanded by Meili itself; 'devops' -> 'devops engineer' is NOT in JOBS_SYNONYMS (case 15).
_notes.notFilters: Seniority (1, 9, 11, 18, 19, 20, 26) is deliberately not a filter (query-understanding.ts header: the corpus is 76% 'mid'). Visa (27), 'anywhere in Europe' (6), 'series B' (11), 'at Shopify' (16), 'summer' (19) are not parsed here.
_notes.mentions: Negations (5, 14, 31) cannot be filters (no Meili negation in buildFilter or the q builder), so they leave the query and are reported. First-person experience (23) is reported, never a filter.
_notes.work_type: Comes from the existing parseWorkTypeTokens; '3-5 yrs' style and 'only please' leftovers are its residue, not new behaviour (23).
_notes.salary: salaryMin is compared RAW against salary_max/salary_min in buildFilter; currency words (CAD, GBP, USD) are consumed and ignored.
_notes.temporary: 'temporary' has no EMPLOYMENT_TYPES value, so it stays in the query.
